newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA BEGINS RE-EVALUATING DEBT MARKET-MAKING.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA BEGINS RE-EVALUATING DEBT MARKET-MAKING.

text.p: The South African Finance Deparment has invited market comment on its re-evaluation of market-making in government bonds.
The move follows Finance Director General Maria Ramos' announcement on March 19 this year that government was rethinking its role in making a market in its debt.

"Both government and the (Reserve) Bank have never been comfortable with the dual role that the Bank has to play as monetary authority on the one hand as as market-maker in government bonds on the other hand," the department said in a statement.

Since the central bank began limiting both its high profile and risk exposure in terms of market-making, its turnover relative to total turnover on the Bond Exchange has declined from 30 percent in 1993 to 18 percent in 1994, nine percent in 1995 and six percent in the first half of 1996.

The department said market participants had been invited to present their views to the department by October 31. This would be followed by a workshop attended by the department, the Reserve Bank and potential market-makers.

"We want to get a flavour of what it is that potential primary dealers would want us to do in terms of market reform and market development to be prepared to assume that role," said Coen Kruger, chief director of sectoral policy and public debt.

He said that once the department had reached a point where it began to appoint primary dealers, it would decide on guidelines which would include prudency criteria, efficiency and general support of the variety of benchmark instruments that would be marketed.
"One of the biggest obstacles historically has been that the asset and reserve positions of banks need to be sound to take the inherent risk in market-making," Kruger said.
In this context, Kruger said it was possible that foreign players could become market-makers.
"It is quite possible that we will have foreign participation as well because the very big international banks' assets and reserves positions are such that they might be interested."
Kruger added that the process of re-evaluating its market-making activities formed part of government's plan to improve its overall debt management policy.
